title: fix(plugin-auth)!: an origin an SSO register or update body names is trusted for that provider's discovery only
body:
Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no skill under `skills/**` teaches trusted origins or SSO provider registration; `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx` gains the rule in this change.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:SSO 注册/更新请求体里写的 issuer 与 oidcConfig 端点的来源(origin),只在该提供方的服务端发现与校验时被信任(注册时的发现与端点校验,以及注册/更新打开“同时退出公司登录”时对登出端点本身的判定;为找该端点而读取的发现文档仍只按部署配置的可信来源),不再计入这次请求本身的来源校验;来源校验只认部署配置的可信来源,与其它 POST 一致。
- 为什么改:请求体给出的来源只该服务于发现校验,请求自身的来源校验应当只看部署配置。
- 风险与回滚:两处收紧(均属 BREAKING,见 changeset)。一:在未被信任的来源的浏览器页面上注册/更新 SSO 提供方,会被 403 INVALID_ORIGIN 拒绝;从控制台或配置来源发起不受这一处影响。二:为内网/私有网络上、其来源未列入部署可信来源的 OIDC 身份提供方打开“同时退出公司登录”(注册或更新),main 上会保存,现在被 400 VALIDATION_FAILED(signOutOfIdp)拒绝,即便从控制台发起;处理办法是把该提供方的来源加入 `OS_TRUSTED_ORIGINS`。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-auth-instance.ts`(可信来源列表不再是按请求的函数)、`src/auth-manager.ts`(`assertSsoSignOutOfIdpSupported` 只把请求体来源交给登出端点判定)、`src/sso-sign-out-of-idp.ts`、`src/sso-discovery-companion-origins.ts`。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/sso-discovery-companion-origins.test.ts src/sso-sign-out-of-idp.test.ts`,预期两文件全部通过(前者 27 例)。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

**Rule.** An origin taken from an SSO register or update request body is trusted only for the server-side discovery fetch and validation of that provider. It never becomes an accepted `Origin` for the request's own origin check, which sees exactly the deployment's configured trusted origins, as on any other POST.

- `auth-manager-auth-instance.ts`: the auth instance's `trustedOrigins` option is the configured list with the SSO relying party wired too; it is no longer a per-request function.
- `auth-manager.ts`: `ssoDiscoveryTrustedOrigins` reads the parsed body (the same issuer and `oidcConfig` endpoints, public-routable hosts only) instead of the raw request. It is the one definition of the body-named set, and two server-side readers of the provider take it: the vendor's discovery and validation, and the sign-out check's logout-endpoint verdict:
  - the vendor's `/sso/register` discovery and endpoint validation: the global before-hook (`auth-manager-before-hook.ts`) hands the set, with the existing companion origins, to that endpoint as a per-endpoint context change (`ssoDiscoveryCompanionContext`). This is the seam the companion origins already use: the vendor merges it into the endpoint's own context after its router-level origin check has run;
  - the sign-out capability check (`assertSsoSignOutOfIdpSupported`) on `/sso/register` and `/sso/update-provider`, when the request turns `signOutOfIdp` on: its verdict on the provider's OIDC logout endpoint alone trusts the body-named set beside the configured list, through `trustingBodyNamedOrigins` (`sso-discovery-companion-origins.ts`), an exact-origin match the same as the vendor's. `judgeSignOutOfIdpCapability` (`sso-sign-out-of-idp.ts`) takes that predicate as a separate input, `isTrustedLogoutOrigin`; the discovery document it reads to find the endpoint is fetched under the configured trust (`isTrustedOrigin`).
- The vendor's `/sso/update-provider` endpoint itself fetches no discovery document, and its endpoint validation admits any public-routable host on its own, so the body-named set (public-routable only) changes none of that endpoint's verdicts. The sign-out capability check's logout-endpoint verdict on update is the one reader there, and it takes the set as above.
- A second, declared narrowing: holding the sign-out check's discovery read to the configured trust means a registration or an update that turns `signOutOfIdp` on for an OIDC identity provider on a private network is refused `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` on `signOutOfIdp` until that provider's origin is in the deployment's trusted origins (`OS_TRUSTED_ORIGINS`, or the `trustedOrigins` option). `main` saved it. The changeset declares it under "Who moves, too".
- `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx`: states the rule, which checks read a body-named origin on each door, and that the sign-out check's discovery read keeps the configured trust.
- `.changeset/sso-body-origins-trust-discovery-only.md`: `patch`, BREAKING, with "Who moves" and the ADR-0087 `not-required` marker.

## Tests

`src/sso-discovery-companion-origins.test.ts`, a top-level describe in the shared harness (a real `AuthManager` with the real `sso()` plugin over the in-memory engine, the origin check on as a deployment runs it):

- register: an `Origin` equal to the body-named issuer is refused by the origin check (`403 INVALID_ORIGIN`); no provider row is written;
- register: an `Origin` equal to a body-named `oidcConfig` endpoint's host is refused; no row is written;
- update: an `Origin` equal to a body-named host is refused, for an endpoint and for an issuer; the provider row is unchanged;
- with `signOutOfIdp` on, an `Origin` equal to a body-named host is still refused, on register and on update; nothing is written or changed;
- the sign-out check's logout-endpoint verdict trusts a body-named origin: a configured-origin register with the switch on saves, keeping the logout endpoint;
- the same for a configured-origin update with the switch on;
- CONTROL: the sign-out capability check still refuses a logout endpoint on a host the body does not name (`400 VALIDATION_FAILED` on `signOutOfIdp`), on register (nothing is written) and on update (the row is unchanged);
- the sign-out capability check trusts a body-named origin for the logout endpoint only: for a provider on a private network whose origin the deployment does not list, a configured-origin register with the switch on is refused `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` on `signOutOfIdp` and nothing is written;
- the same on update; the row is unchanged;
- CONTROL: with that origin listed in the deployment's trusted origins, the same register saves and keeps the logout endpoint;
- CONTROL: the same request naming a different host is refused by the origin check too;
- CONTROL: a same-origin register naming an external issuer and a foreign endpoint still discovers and registers;
- CONTROL: a same-origin register whose discovery names an endpoint the body does not is still refused `discovery_untrusted_origin`;
- CONTROL: a same-origin update naming a foreign endpoint still validates and is saved;
- CONTROL: another POST is judged against the configured origins alone.

Every switch-on case installs the identity provider's whole test environment (its discovery documents and its network placement), so none leans on the runner's own environment.

In the companion-origin table describe: the logout-endpoint verdict's predicate, `trustingBodyNamedOrigins`, admits a body-named origin by exact origin only (another port, scheme, subdomain or protocol, or a non-URL, is refused), and with no body-named origin it is the request's own predicate.

`src/sso-sign-out-of-idp.test.ts`: `judgeSignOutOfIdpCapability` with `isTrustedLogoutOrigin` given accepts a logout endpoint on the origin only that predicate trusts, while its discovery fetch receives `isTrustedOrigin`; with it absent, the same endpoint is refused on `signOutOfIdp` (the verdict falls back to `isTrustedOrigin`).

`src/auth-manager.test.ts`: the SSO-wired pins assert the configured list (production with a list, production with none: key omitted, non-production: the localhost trio), never a function.

## Acceptance notes

- The before-hook host gains one member (`ssoDiscoveryTrustedOrigins`), and the auth-instance host drops `isSsoWired`, which nothing there reads any more.
- `register-sso-provider.ts` comments were re-read and still state the rule (an endpoint the registration names is trusted for that registration); no change.
- `origin/main` was merged before the PR opened (at `dc13f5644e`). The round-2 commits were not followed by another merge: the commits on `main` since then touch neither `plugin-auth` nor its dependency closure, and there is no conflict.

## Verification

Readings at head `027821da02`, unless a line names another commit. Source is unchanged since `7a02d7506a`; the commit after it changes tests, docs and the changeset only.

`vitest run src/sso-discovery-companion-origins.test.ts`: 3 failed, 15 passed. The three request-origin rule tests were red (each answered `200` where `403` is required), and every CONTROL was green, including the different-host refusal.

</details>

<details><summary>Sign-out capability tests before the round-2 fix (commit dc13f5644e plus the new tests)</summary>

`vitest run src/sso-discovery-companion-origins.test.ts`: 2 failed, 20 passed. The configured-origin register and update with the switch on were both refused `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` on `signOutOfIdp`; the CONTROL for a logout endpoint on a host the body does not name, and the request-origin refusals with the switch on, were green.

</details>

<details><summary>Logout-endpoint-only narrowing, measured before the fix (CI at commit 18b8af0cea, the pins-first commit)</summary>

`Test Core (7/8)` on `18b8af0cea`: plugin-auth 3 failed, 5538 passed. The two limit pins answered `200` where `400` is required: before the limit, turning the switch on for a provider on a private network whose origin the deployment does not list was saved on both doors, as on `main`. That is the verdict the changeset declares under "Who moves, too". The third red was the update-door CONTROL's own setup (its registration's discovery document published the foreign logout endpoint, which the vendor's register discovery refuses); the CONTROL now registers before that endpoint is published.

</details>

Restored: blob equals HEAD (`14c267f6a2ac`), marker count 0, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- Sign-out capability hand-off, before it was limited (at `f87435b23a`): mutation in `auth-manager.ts`, giving the capability check no body-named origins.
